summary:
RSAS (Rhizosphere-Spray Agrivoltaic System) is a closed-loop agricultural system that helps farms adapt to compound climate stresses — drought, heat, and frost — by unifying three technologies under one NASA-data-driven decision layer.

The problem: the same field now faces all three stresses in a single growing cycle, and conventional agriculture responds to each separately — usually too late. A single frost night during flowering can destroy up to 35% of an orchard's flowers.

Our solution has three pillars. Rhizosphere Engineering (RE 2.0) uses NASA POWER, SMAP and MODIS data fused with IoT sensors to predict a stress event 3–7 days ahead and pre-design synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) tuned to that stress — including cold-adapted strains that secrete antifreeze proteins. SMART SPRAY is a biodegradable polymer spray that fixes those microbes to the root zone, preserves soil moisture, and insulates plants against frost. Dynamic Agrivoltaics autonomously tilts panels: shading crops in heatwaves (3–4 °C reduction, 41–42% water savings) and rotating horizontal on frost nights to keep plant surfaces above freezing.

Frost defense is four-layered: prediction, biological, physical, and structural. A 1-hectare pilot costs ~$1.1–1.5M USD, offset by €100–200K/ha/year in energy revenue. RSAS is at proof-of-concept level; an interactive bilingual prototype with a live cost calculator is available.
details:
PROJECT OVERVIEW

RSAS (Rhizosphere-Spray Agrivoltaic System) is a closed-loop agricultural system that helps farms adapt to compound climate stresses by unifying three independently validated technologies under one NASA-data-driven decision layer. The project was developed for the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge.

THE PROBLEM

Climate change no longer delivers stresses one at a time. A single field now encounters drought, heatwaves, and frost within the same growing cycle. Conventional agriculture treats each stress separately and reactively:

- Drought collapses both soil moisture and the rhizosphere microbiome the plant depends on.

- Heatwaves accelerate evaporation and respiration losses; yield damage can be irreversible.

- A single frost night during flowering can destroy up to 35% of a fruit orchard's flowers.

By the time a farmer observes the damage, the intervention window has already closed. The core problem is not a lack of technology — it is a lack of coordination and early warning.

OUR SOLUTION: THREE PILLARS, ONE CLOSED LOOP

1. Rhizosphere Engineering (RE 2.0)

Conventional microbial fertilizers add microorganisms to soil at random. RE 2.0 does the opposite: it pre-designs synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) that best respond to the plant's root exudates under a specific climate stress. Using NASA POWER (meteorology), SMAP (soil moisture), and MODIS (vegetation health, land surface temperature) fused with field IoT sensors, the system predicts a stress event 3–7 days ahead and prescribes the matching SynCom composition. In frost scenarios, cold-adapted strains such as Pseudomonas putida GR12-2 — which survives at -20 °C and even -50 °C by secreting antifreeze proteins — are deployed to the root zone.

2. SMART SPRAY

A biodegradable polymer spray whose primary purpose is NOT to sprinkle water. It is the system's carrier and protective layer: it fixes the engineered SynComs to the root zone, preserves soil moisture (up to 35% retention), reduces evaporation, and forms a protective film on the plant surface that provides thermal insulation against frost. It fully decomposes in 5–7 months.

3. Dynamic Agrivoltaics

Solar panels whose tilt is autonomously adjusted based on real-time NASA data. During heatwaves they shade crops, reducing peak temperatures by 3–4 °C and cutting water use by 41–42%. On frost-risk nights they rotate to horizontal, reducing radiative cooling — keeping plant surface temperatures positive while control plots drop to -3 °C.

Together, these three pillars make frost defense four-layered and independent: prediction (satellite early warning) + biological (antifreeze proteins) + physical (polymer film) + structural (panel blanket).

HOW NASA DATA DRIVES THE SYSTEM

RSAS runs a continuous closed loop rather than a one-way pipeline:

NASA POWER, SMAP, and MODIS data plus in-field IoT sensors feed an AI layer that predicts upcoming stress events and prescribes SynCom composition, spray timing, and panel angles. IoT sensors then measure outcomes and feed back into the model, which updates itself continuously.

Data sources used:

- NASA POWER — solar and meteorological data for agricultural modeling and irrigation planning

- SMAP — soil moisture

- MODIS — NDVI, EVI, LAI, evapotranspiration, land surface temperature

WHAT MAKES THIS NOVEL

Each component exists separately in the literature. The novelty is the integration. No published system unifies rhizosphere engineering, biodegradable polymer sprays, and dynamic agrivoltaics into a single closed loop governed by real-time NASA Earth observation data. RSAS also serves as a concept model for future lunar and Martian greenhouses, where a "data-governed rhizosphere" replaces open soil.

FEASIBILITY AND ECONOMICS

A 1-hectare pilot is estimated at $1.1–1.5M USD. The largest item is the dynamic agrivoltaic structure (~€1M/ha, roughly three times a fixed solar installation), but that same structure also generates electricity: €100,000–200,000 per hectare per year. In the French vineyard case study, the farmer pays nothing upfront and leases the land instead, so the investment is carried by the energy side. USD and EUR are reported separately; no currency conversion has been performed.

Component-level estimates per hectare:

- Dynamic agrivoltaic structure: ~€1,000,000

- SMART SPRAY polymer: $650–4,500

- SynComs: $20–50

- IoT sensor infrastructure: $500–2,000

IMPACT

- 3–4 °C peak temperature reduction during heatwaves

- 41–42% water savings

- 0.27–0.47 °C higher air temperature on frost nights; 1.61–1.69 °C protection at the flower bud

- Frost-damaged flower rate reduced from 35% to below 10%

- Estimated simple payback period of 5.5–15 years (excluding O&M, financing, and taxes)

PROTOTYPE

We built an interactive bilingual (Turkish/English) prototype website featuring:

- An interactive architecture diagram linking each pillar to its section

- A live data-loop animation with play/pause controls and per-step navigation

- Animated impact metric counters

- A working cost calculator: adjust the hectare slider and all cost and revenue estimates update live

- A fully referenced bibliography of 22 sources across 7 categories

STATUS AND HONESTY NOTE

RSAS is currently at the proof-of-concept and simulation level. Each component is grounded in peer-reviewed literature, but the full closed loop has not yet been field-tested at commercial scale. We present this as a scientifically grounded concept and a working interactive prototype, not as a validated commercial product.

TEAM

RSAS Team — Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.
